verses.45:2: O nosso Deus é refúgio e {virtus}: * {adjutor} nas tribulações que {nimis} nos encontraram.
verses.45:3: Por isso não temeremos enquanto a terra for perturbada: * {transferentur} para o coração do mar.
verses.45:4: {sonuerunt}, e se perturbaram {aquae}: * os montes se perturbaram {fortitudine}.
verses.45:5: O ímpeto do rio alegra a cidade de Deus: * o Altíssimo santificou {tabernaculum}.
verses.45:6: Deus está no meio dela, {commovebitur}: * Deus a auxiliará {mane}.
verses.45:7: As nações se perturbaram, e os reinos {inclinata}: * fez ouvir a sua voz, a terra se abalou.
verses.45:8: O Senhor {virtutum} está conosco: * o nosso amparo é o Deus de Jacó.
verses.45:9: Vinde, e vede as obras do Senhor, {prodigia} sobre a terra: * {auferens} as guerras até {finem} da terra.
verses.45:10: {conteret} o arco, e {confringet} as armas: * e queimará os escudos no fogo.
verses.45:11: {vacate}, e vede que eu sou Deus: * serei exaltado entre as nações, e serei exaltado na terra.
verses.45:12: O Senhor {virtutum} está conosco: * o nosso amparo é o Deus de Jacó.

decisions.why: virtus of God → *poder* (row; 20:2 *no vosso poder*, 28:11). Everyone knows the line as 'refúgio e força' (DRB 'strength', MS1932 *força*), but *força* is fortitúdo's (row), and fortitúdo stands two verses later in this psalm (45:4 *in fortitúdine ejus*): the Latin's two words stay two. The Latin has one *noster*, on *Deus*; the predicate nouns stand bare, as 9:10 *se fez refúgio*. MS1932 moves the possessive (*Deus é nosso refúgio e nossa força*); DRB adds a second 'our'.

options.label: poder
options.note: Ruling: the row; keeps 45:4's fortitúdo → força apart.

options.label: força
options.note: DRB, MS1932; the familiar line; merges virtus with fortitúdo (45:4).

decisions.why: adjútor → *auxílio* (row, uniform in 14 places, open for Gustavo); here in apposition to *Deus*, as 9:10 *auxílio nas horas oportunas, na tribulação*. The Latinist has repeatedly asked for the agent noun *auxiliador*; the row records why it is refused (length, currency, the psalter's one word). tribulátio → *tribulação* (row).

options.label: auxiliador
options.note: the agent noun, as the Latin; the Latinist's standing request elsewhere.

decisions.why: *nimis* (σφόδρα) goes with the verb: the troubles found us 'exceedingly' (DRB). The glossary has no one rendering; 37:9 *humiliátus sum nimis* → *humilhado sem medida* (L&S 'beyond measure'), 118:96 → *muito*. *sem medida* is put before the verb so that the colon ends on *encontraram* (paroxytone), and so that it is not heard as the manner of finding. invenire → *encontrar*, as 118:143 *Tribulátio … invenérunt me* → *me encontraram*. MS1932 paraphrases (*que nos cercavam de todas as partes*).

options.label: muito
options.note: 118:96's word; *que muito nos encontraram* is weak.

decisions.latin: et transferéntur montes in cor maris
decisions.why: Two things. (1) Scope: the Greek has both verbs as infinitives under one ἐν τῷ ('when the earth is troubled and the mountains are moved'), and DRB keeps them in one clause; so the second colon continues *enquanto*, with the Portuguese future subjunctive (*forem*). (2) The verb: transférre, 'carry across, remove' (L&S); μετατίθεσθαι. *transportar* is the plain word that keeps the carrying; *transferidos* is an office's word in Brazil; MS1932 *trasladados* is little used outside the moving of relics and bodies; DRB 'removed'. *in cor maris* → *para o coração do mar* — the Latin's heart kept (MS1932's *para o meio do mar* flattens the image).

options.label: e os montes forem transportados
options.note: Ruling: one clause with *enquanto*, as the Greek and DRB.

options.label: e os montes serão transportados
options.note: the Latin's indicative read as a main clause; a prophecy the Latin does not clearly make.

decisions.why: sonáre, 'to sound, resound'; ἤχησαν. *Ressoaram* keeps the Latin's plain verb of sound. MS1932 *Bramaram* and DRB 'roared' make it the roar of the sea, which the context allows but the word does not say.

options.label: Bramaram
options.note: MS1932; the roar, stronger than the Latin.

decisions.why: *eórum* is plural; in the Latin the only plural in sight is *montes* (the Greek's 'hearts of the seas' is plural, the Latin's *cor maris* is not), so the waters are grammatically the mountains' — though the image is the sea's. *as águas deles* ties them to the mountains outright; *as suas águas* (MS1932) leaves the owner to the listener, which is as open as the Latin is to the ear. turbáre → *perturbar* (row); MS1932 *turbaram-se*.

options.label: as águas deles
options.note: the Latin's plural pointer made explicit (the mountains).

decisions.latin: conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine ejus
decisions.why: *ejus* is singular — God's (DRB 'his strength'), or the sea's; not the mountains' own (that would be *eórum*/*sua*). *in* + ablative with a verb of being shaken is 'by / with' (DRB 'with', MS1932 *pela sua fortaleza*); *perturbar-se com* is the Portuguese of being shaken by something. fortitúdo → *força* (row), kept apart from 45:2 virtus → poder. *com a força dele* would pin a masculine singular (God or the sea — still the Latin's two) but is heavy.

options.label: na sua força
options.note: the preposition calqued; can be heard as the mountains 'in their strength'.

options.label: com a força dele
options.note: excludes the mountains' own strength; heavier.

decisions.why: tabernáculum → *tenda* (row, open; 14:1, 18:6a, 42:3). **For Gustavo's ear:** this colon is sung alone of the Blessed Virgin — antiphon *Adjúvit eam Deus mane dilúculo; sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus* at the Immaculate Conception (Sancti/12-08) and Our Lady Aparecida (Brasilia/10-12), a versicle for Dedication (12-10-Domus) and the Commons (C6-1) — found with ps032/uses.py. There the tabernacle is Mary, and a Brazilian ear hears *tabernáculo* as the place of the Presence, which is exactly that sense; *tenda* keeps the Latin's image and the psalter's one word. MS1932 *tabernáculo*.

options.label: o seu tabernáculo
options.note: MS1932; the Marian reading of the antiphons.

decisions.latin: Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur
decisions.why: The Latin gives no subject: the city (Greek and Hebrew, feminine) or God just named. A Portuguese participle must choose a gender (*abalada* the city, MS1932 *não será comovida*; *abalado* God, as 20:8 *não será abalado*); the pronominal *não se abalará* chooses neither and keeps the verb (commovére → *abalar*, 17:8, 20:8, 28:7). It also reads alone, as the Commons of Virgins and of the Virgin sing it (*Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur*, C6, C6-1, 08-15t, 12-13).

options.label: não se abalará
options.note: Ruling: keeps the Latin's open subject.

options.label: não será abalada
options.note: the city, as the Greek; MS1932 *comovida*.

decisions.why: Two Latin words for early morning (τὸ πρὸς πρωί, one phrase in Greek): mane → *de manhã* (row, 5:4–5), dilúculum → *ao amanhecer* (row, 118:148). Both kept: the Latin's doubling is its own, and the colon is sung alone as a Marian antiphon (12-08, Aparecida). DRB 'in the morning early'; MS1932 *desde o raiar da manhã* (one phrase).

inclináre, 'bend, bow, sink' (ἔκλιναν, 'gave way'); DRB 'were bowed down'. *se inclinaram* keeps the verb the psalter has for *inclína aurem* (→ *inclinai*); it can be heard as bowing in homage, which the Latin's word also allows. MS1932 *se humilharam* interprets.

options.label: vacilaram
options.note: the Greek's giving way; loses the Latin's bending.

decisions.why: *Dóminus virtútum* → *o Senhor dos poderes* (formula row, open; 23:10 applied, passed the Latinist twice; its row asked for a ruling 'before Ps 45', which has not been made). κύριος τῶν δυνάμεων: the Latin says powers, as the Greek does; *dos exércitos* is the Hebrew's Sabaoth (DRB 'armies', MS1932 *dos exércitos*) and is how the verse is known in Brazil. The refrain is also the Matins versicle *V. Dóminus virtútum nobíscum* (Psalmi matutinum) and reads alone. *nobíscum* needs a verb: *está* supplied (D2). 45:8 = 45:12, one slot.

options.label: dos exércitos
options.note: DRB, MS1932; the familiar form; the Hebrew's image.

options.label: das virtudes
options.note: the cognate; *virtude* is a moral quality today.

decisions.latin: ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram
decisions.why: *quæ … prodígia* can be a relative with its noun drawn in ('the wonders which he set'), an exclamation (DRB 'what wonders he hath done'), or, as the Greek ἃ ἔθετο τέρατα, 'the works which he set as wonders'. MS1932 builds the apposition (*as maravilhas que operou*); it is the reading that keeps both nouns and reads without a gloss. pónere → *pôr* (the Latin's plain verb; MS1932 *operou*, DRB 'done' soften it). prodígium → *prodígio*.

options.label: que prodígios pôs
options.note: DRB's exclamation; *que* after *Senhor* can be heard as a relative.

decisions.why: auferre → *tirar* (settled, D41); the participle as a gerund, as the Latin hangs it on *Dómini*. ἀνταναιρῶν, 'taking away'. DRB 'making wars to cease' and MS1932 *fazendo cessar* say the result, not the Latin's verb.

options.label: fazendo cessar
options.note: DRB, MS1932; the result, not the verb.

decisions.why: *finem* is singular, 'the end, the edge' of the earth (μέχρι τῶν περάτων, plural in the Greek). *os confins* is kept for *fines terræ* (21:28, plural). *até o fim da terra* keeps the Latin's number; it could be heard as time ('till the end of the world'), which the ambiguity reader should test. MS1932 *até à extremidade do mundo*.

The glossary gives both contérere and confríngere *quebrar* (one Greek verb in 2:9 / 3:8) and names this verse as the place that 'must decide locally'. Here the Greek has two verbs too, τόξον συντρίψει καὶ συγκλάσει ὅπλον — so by D15's test the two stay two: contérere keeps the row's *quebrar* (3:8, 9:36 *Quebrai o braço*), and confríngere takes the row's named option *despedaçar* (MS1932 *fará em pedaços*). Natural order, the verb first (D2).

options.label: Quebrará … despedaçará
options.note: Ruling: two Greek verbs, two Portuguese; MS1932.

options.label: Quebrará … quebrará
options.note: both rows as written; repeats a verb the Latin varies.

options.label: Despedaçará … quebrará
options.note: the pair the other way round; confríngere keeps *quebrar* as 2:9, 17:39, 28:5.

decisions.why: vacáre: 'be empty, free from; be free from labour, at leisure' (L&S); σχολάσατε, 'cease, have leisure'. *Parai* is plain, is MS1932's, and is safe under rule 3 (past *parei*). *Aquietai-vos* is DRB's 'be still' (and the Hebrew's 'let go'), a softer, inward stillness. The Latin word's monastic resonance (to be free for God) is not in any one Portuguese verb. God speaks to a plural audience: *vós*. *vidéte* → *vede*, as 45:9 — the repetition kept (MS1932 varies it to *reconhecei*).

options.label: Descansai
options.note: the leisure sense; loses the ceasing.

choices.45:2: *Deus noster* → *O nosso Deus* (article before the possessive). refúgium → *refúgio* (row; 31:7, 90:2). *nas tribulações* for *in tribulatiónibus* (plural kept). The whole verse is sung for the Protomartyrs of Rome (Sancti/Urbis/06-27).
choices.45:4: turbáre and conturbáre both → *perturbar* (rows; ταράσσω both times) — the Latin's near-repetition kept as one verb twice. Natural order in the second colon (the subject first), a copy of 17:8 *os fundamentos dos montes se perturbaram*.
choices.45:5: *Flúminis ímpetus* → *O ímpeto do rio* (ὁρμήματα, 'rushings'; the cognate is current; DRB 'stream' and MS1932 *um rio caudaloso* take the force out of the noun). lætificáre → *alegrar* (row; 42:4). *cívitas Dei* → *a cidade de Deus*. Altíssimus → *o Altíssimo* (row); the verb-subject order of the Latin turned to natural order so the colon ends on a paroxytone. Both colons are sung alone as versicles (C6-1, 02-05 missa, Brasilia/08-30) and read alone.
choices.45:6: *Deus in médio ejus* → *Deus está no meio dela* (copula supplied, D2); *ejus* is the city. adjuváre → *auxiliar* (row), *Deus a auxiliará*. The second colon is the Marian antiphon *Adjúvit eam Deus mane dilúculo* (with a perfect there — the psalm keeps its future).
choices.45:7: conturbáre → *perturbar* (row). *dedit vocem suam* → *fez ouvir a sua voz* (row; 17:14); the subject left unnamed, as the Latin (MS1932 supplies *Deus*). *mota est terra* → *a terra se abalou* (movére → *abalar*, as 17:8 *Commóta est … terra* → *A terra se abalou*); the Latin's asyndeton kept.
choices.45:8: suscéptor → *amparo* (D19); *noster* → *o nosso*. *Deus Jacob* → *o Deus de Jacó* (19:2, 23:6). The Latin's order (the title first, the name last) kept, with *é* supplied: the colon ends on the name, as the Latin does. = 45:12 word for word (a refrain; the brief).
choices.45:9: *Veníte, et vidéte* → *Vinde, e vede* (33:12 *Vinde*; 33:9 *vede*). *ópera Dómini* → *as obras do Senhor* (27:5, 117:17). *super terram* → *sobre a terra*. The first colon is long in the Latin too.
choices.45:10: *scuta* plural → *os escudos*; *combúret igni* → *queimará … no fogo* (DRB 'in the fire'); the Latin puts the object first, Portuguese order puts the verb first (D2). *arma* → *as armas*.
choices.45:11: God speaks: *eu sou Deus* (no article; MS1932 *o Deus* follows the Greek's ὁ θεός; the Latin has none). exaltáre → *exaltar* (row); *exaltábor … et exaltábor* → *serei exaltado … e serei exaltado*, the repetition kept. *in géntibus* → *entre as nações* (gentes → nações, row); *in terra* → *na terra*.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm45.txt, 11 prayed verses (45:2–45:12; no titulus, D7). One mediant per verse, no flex. Not a day-hours psalm: no DM1962 column. Uses by grep (ps032/uses.py): 45:5 whole as a versicle (C6-1, missa 02-05, Brasilia/08-30), 45:5b and 45:6b as the Marian antiphon of the Immaculate Conception and Our Lady Aparecida, 45:6a in the Commons of Virgins and of the BVM, 45:8a as the Matins versicle, 45:2 whole for the Protomartyrs (Urbis/06-27). So these colons must read alone.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps045.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Formulas checked with ps038/xref.py. Rules applied: D19 (suscéptor → amparo), D41 (auferre → tirar), rows virtus → poder (God's), fortitúdo → força, adjútor → auxílio, (con)turbáre → perturbar, (com)movére → abalar, vocem dare, tabernáculum → tenda, mane / dilúculo, gentes → nações, *Dóminus virtútum* → *o Senhor dos poderes* (formula row, unruled). Local rulings: contérere / confríngere kept apart here (two Greek verbs), *não se abalará* (keeps the Latin's open subject), *Parai* for vacáte. Refrain 45:8 = 45:12 built from one slot. Tests for the readers: *refúgio e poder*, *sem medida nos encontraram*, *as suas águas*, *com a sua força*, *a sua tenda*, *tirando as guerras até o fim da terra*, *Parai*.

Draft 1: hard pass. Length flags accepted: 45:3 +4/+7 (the Portuguese future subjunctive passive *for perturbada … forem transportados* has no short form; *levados* would take addúcere's verb, D42); 45:8 = 45:12 +3/+3 (the copulas *está*, *é* the verbless Latin lacks); 45:10 +4/+3 (*despedaçará*, the second verb kept apart); 45:11 −6/+5 (*Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam* is long Latin for *Parai, e vede que*; the second colon keeps the Latin's *exaltábor … exaltábor*); 45:9a −3. Rhyme flag 45:9 *terra … terra*: the Latin has the same echo (*terram … terræ*), allowed by rule 5. Oxytone cadences where the Latin is paroxytone at 45:2a *poder*, 45:5a *Deus*, 45:6 *abalará*, *amanhecer*, 45:7b *abalou*, 45:8b = 45:12b *Jacó* — each the Latin's own word or the verb the row gives; allowed by rule 4.
